instruction: Offset-and-extrude walls from a closed footprint Read `C:\Users\user\Desktop\footprint.json`. The file specifies an L-shaped footprint via `corners` (a list of `[x, y]` points in meters, in CCW order forming a closed outline), a `thickness_m` (wall thickness, inward offset), and a `height_m` (wall extrusion height). Build 3D walls by: 1. Offsetting the footprint polygon inward by `thickness_m`. 2. Extruding the resulting annulus (outer boundary minus inner boundary) from Z=0 to Z=`height_m`. Save the native SketchUp model to `C:\Users\user\Desktop\answer.skp`. Requirements: 1. `C:\Users\user\Desktop\answer.skp` can be opened and inspected as a native SketchUp model. 2. Bounding box X span approx span of input corners, within 10 mm. 3. Bounding box Y span approx span of input corners, within 10 mm. 4. Bounding box Z span approx `height_m`, within 2 mm. 5. Number of vertices >= 16 (outer + inner loops x 2 heights). [Software] Launch SketchUp with `C:\SketchUp 2026 26.0.429 x64 En Portable\SketchUp.exe` (adjust if your install differs).
